Variants.Content: Rivers and bays turn war into a contest of ships, tides, winds, quays, and supply. River warfare fights over fords, bridges, and grain barges; naval warfare relies on fleets, harbors, sailors who know hidden reefs, and hinterlands able to supply timber and sailcloth continually. Ironborn longships are suited to shallows and swift raids, whereas royal and Reach fleets depend more on harbors, tax revenues, and great shipyards, while wildfire, fireships, and blockades can shift the balance of strength. Sailors care about weather and cordage, lords care about sea lanes and customs dues, and common folk care whether fishing boats can still put to sea.
